message.content:
**Rough estimate – about 4–6 weeks** Here’s how I got there: | Step | What we know | How we calculate | |------|--------------|------------------| | **Surface area** | The tower’s exposed metal surface is roughly 10 000 m² (≈ 107 000 ft²).
*(Source: Wikipedia “Eiffel Tower”)* | | | **Paint coverage** | A typical industrial spray‑paint or roller job covers ≈ 10 m² per litre (≈ 110 ft²/litre). | | | **Litres required** | 10 000 m² ÷ 10 m²/litre ≈ **1 000 litres** of paint. | | **Crew productivity** | A skilled crew can apply ≈ 200 l/day (≈ 22 ft²/min) when working continuously on a single section.
*(Industry standard for large‑scale façade work)* | | | **Days of work** | 1 000 l ÷ 200 l/day ≈ **5 days** of active spraying/rolling. | | **Practical constraints** | • Weather delays (rain, wind, temperature extremes).
• Safety inspections between sections.
• Time to set up scaffolding, ladders, and protective gear.
• Multiple crews may work simultaneously but still need to coordinate. | | Putting all that together, you get something like: * **Active paint‑application time:** ~5 days (≈ 40 hours of work if each crew works 8 h/day). * **Total calendar time including setup, inspection, and weather windows:** **4–6 weeks**. So while the actual “painting” might only take a few days of continuous effort, the whole project—planning, scaffolding, safety checks, and dealing with the inevitable rain—usually stretches out over a month or more.
